# ANALYSIS: WEEKLY-1-DTE-REAL-FILLS-WF-2026Q3-DISCREPANCY

## Hypothesis

The leaderboard claims that the weekly-1 DTE signal (1-2 DTE) has an OOS expectancy of $59-66 per trade (see WEEKLY_DTE_NOT_0DTE candidate). However, a BS-synthetic walk-forward on 2026-Q3 held-out shows a negative expectancy of -$6.51 per trade and a win rate of 18.7%. We hypothesize that the discrepancy may stem from: (a) the leaderboard's OOS test covering a different time period, (b) BS-synthetic pricing not matching real OPRA fills, or (c) regime-specific performance decay in 2026-Q3.

## Mechanism

We executed a walk-forward evaluation of the weekly-1 DTE signal (as implied by the WEEKLY_DTE_NOT_0DTE candidate) over 2026-Q3 (July-September 2026) as the held-out OOS window. The signal mechanics are not detailed in the leaderboard but are assumed to be a directional bias signal applied at 1-2 DTE with fixed ITM-2 strike and -8%/+30% exit. The evaluation used BS-synthetic option pricing (Black-Scholes) over historical SPY/VIX bars, not real OPRA fills. Outputs include per-trade expectancy, win rate, and OP-16 anchor day breakdown.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** Per-trade expectancy in dollars assumes 1 contract per signal. For account scaling, $1K paper ≈ 14% of headline (qty=28 requires $25K+).  
2. **Sample bias:** Sample = 2026-Q3 held-out window (63 trading days). Signal source: WEEKLY_DTE_NOT_0DTE candidate (filed 2026-07-07), developed pre-July 2026. Overfit risk: signal may be tuned to pre-2026-Q3 regimes.  
3. **Out-of-sample:** BS-synthetic OOS result: expectancy -$6.51/tr, WR 18.7%, edge_capture=759.21 (OP-16 floor=771 → FAIL).
